_sobre: Clothes as cloth on the step-12 body (dress_cloth.py). Values by eye, starting from Blender's cotton and denim presets; mass from the fabric's weight per square metre. Edit to change.
fonte: female_casualsuit01 (MakeHuman system assets, CC0): one mesh, its upper part is the top, the lower the jeans

vestir._sobre: dress_rest.py's pieces (Rafael, 2026-11-15: any garment): piece -> MPFB clothes asset and which of its connected parts: toda, or cima / baixo (above / below the body's waist, spine.001's head)

blusinha._massa: the fabric's real mass (18 mg per vertex) blew Blender's cloth apart in the first frames (test 4, 2026-11-14); 0.3 kg is Blender's cotton preset
blusinha._presa: vertices within this of the neck opening follow the simulated skin (gola e alto dos ombros)

jeans._presa: vertices within this of the waist opening follow the simulated skin (cos)

solver_tetraedros._sobre: the cloth inside the tetrahedral solver (tissue_cloth_sim.py), step 17. Real mass; stiffness of the sheet in N/m, by eye: a T-shirt jersey stretches easily, denim hardly. Contact: the cloth keeps `espessura_mm` from the skin, skin keeps `pele_pele_mm` from skin of another part (arm, trunk, each leg), counted only between points at least `pele_pele_longe_em_repouso_mm` apart at rest (neighbours across a part's border are not contact).
solver_tetraedros._pano_pano: Rafael, 2026-11-15: the cloth has a thickness: each piece's espessura_mm (2 mm for top and jeans) is also kept between cloth and cloth, the top through itself and the top against the jeans. A piece's own triangles within pano_pano_longe_em_repouso_mm of a vertex at rest are its neighbourhood, not contact (by eye, a few of the cloth's edges).

jeans._cos: the waistband (within cos_mm of the waist opening) is tighter: it holds the jeans on the hips; with 2% everywhere they slid 23 mm down in 10 frames (teste_2)

solver_tetraedros._flexao: Thick shell (Rafael, 2026-11-15; tissue_cloth_sim.py flexao=isometrica): bending by Bergou 2006's isometric model with the fabric's measured bending rigidity B (Kawabata KES-FB2, gf cm2/cm; D = B x 9.80665e-5 N m). Knit cotton: 0.002 to 0.050 (US patent 5427156, its range for knit cotton fabric; 0.02 taken, the middle of its preferred 0.003-0.045). Denim: 0.273 (a finished denim of 354 g/m2, Thai Textile journal, li05.tci-thaijo.org article 1056). D = E t^3 / 12(1 - nu^2) with the fabric's tensile modulus would make the jersey ~50 times stiffer than measured: a fabric is yarns, not a solid sheet; the report gives the modulus a solid 2 mm sheet would need. flexao_N_m is used only with flexao=distancia (the way until tet_v10).
